author: Chris Ogden
releaseNotes:
1.4.4 - A safe Reconnect to SignalBricks (#46). The Reconnect link carries the app's access token (Hubitat cloud needs it to route the sign-in back), which is the token the dispatcher uses to send door codes, and an abandoned link left that token in browser history and logs indefinitely. Reconnect is now a button: a click shows Continue to SignalBricks, a sign-in link that works for 10 minutes. Finishing or cancelling the sign-in replaces the token and registers the new one, as before. If no sign-in result arrives within 10 minutes, the app replaces the token and registers the new one with the connection it already has, so the link stops working. Only the token changes: bookings, slot assignments and code writes in progress are kept, door codes keep syncing, and the dispatcher picks up the new token on its next run. A failed registration is retried automatically as before and shown under Status. The expiry survives booking syncs, Reset State and Done. No token is logged, and none is shown on the page except inside the open link.
1.4.3 - A clearer page after Connect or Reconnect to SignalBricks (#40). The page SignalBricks sends you back to was unstyled and read "Connecting", as if it were stuck. It is now a centred card that works on a phone and follows the device's light or dark mode, with a coloured marker and a headline for the outcome: Hub authorized (the app is finishing registration and shows Connected when you reopen it), Not connected (sign-in cancelled or denied), Connect link expired, or Connection failed with the reason. Each failure says what to do next. A Back to the app link opens the app's page on the hub by its local IP address, with a note on where to find the app when you are not on the hub's network. The page is still one self-contained response with no external scripts, fonts or images, and it shows no token, authorization code or other part of the callback URL; an OAuth error from SignalBricks is no longer echoed on it. The connection itself (OAuth, the access token replaced on every callback, registration and its retries), door code writing, reconcile and the refresh are unchanged.
1.4.2 - A failing endpoint no longer logs or returns its exception message (#38). When a request to /sync, /sync/<id>, /devices, /info, /register or another endpoint failed (HTTP 500), the app wrote the exception's message to the log at error level and returned it in the response; for a malformed request body that message can list the body, door codes included. The log line and the response now carry only the handler and the exception's class, e.g. "apiSync failed (MissingMethodException)". A lock event handler error is logged by class only too, and the dormant outbound webhook logs the HTTP status of its response instead of the body. Door code writing, reconcile, the refresh and the connection are unchanged.
1.4.1 - Clearer app page and Bookings page (#36). The app page's section titles (Configuration, Door code refresh, Connection, Diagnostics) and the Debug page's all use the same header style. The Connection section shows one Status line: Connected to <organization> → <hub> since …, Authorized, not registered yet, or Not connected, with the last connect error under it. The App Version line (the name and version are at the top of the page) and the old "Status: Not registered (use CLI add-hub to configure)" block with its note and its Disconnect button are gone; the /register endpoint is unchanged. The cloud URL, local URL and access token are still shown only while the hub is not connected. On the Bookings page each booking has a bold heading (booking id, guest, status, dates and the masked code) with its locks indented under it, and a current booking's "not on lock" is shown in red; for a lock not selected in the app, an upcoming or past booking's line now says "(added at check-in)" or "(removed after checkout)" like the other locks. The Debug page's API links carry the access token, so they are hidden while the hub is connected to SignalBricks (shown as before while it is not). Clicking Done or Reset State clears a leftover ID from the old /register registration, which stops the old outbound webhook to a placeholder address on hubs that still had one, and /register no longer logs its request body. Door codes and the access token are no longer written to the log: with debug or trace logging on, the booking syncs (PUT and PATCH /sync), the device command and device detail endpoints, reconcile and its set, verify and delete jobs, the duplicate-code check and the outbound webhook used to log whole request bodies, bookings, lock code lists or URL parameters, which could include codes and the token. They now log the number of bookings, booking ids, guest names, lock ids and slot numbers only. The duplicate-code error from PUT /sync/<id>/<lock> (HTTP 409) now shows only the code's last 2 digits. Codes still show only their last 2 digits. Door code writing, reconcile, the refresh and the connection are unchanged.
1.4.0 - Connect to SignalBricks (#34). The app page has a Connect to SignalBricks link: sign in to SignalBricks as a door code admin, choose the organization, property and hub, and the app registers the hub's local and cloud addresses and its access token with SignalBricks, so nobody copies URLs and tokens into the dispatcher config any more. It uses OAuth 2.0 with PKCE (S256) through Hubitat's cloud redirect, like SignalBricks Telemetry. Before storing the token SignalBricks verifies it by calling the app through Hubitat cloud, so the hub needs cloud access while it connects; the app registers in the background and shows Connected a few seconds later. Every connect attempt replaces the app's access token (the old one travelled in the connect link): Connect, but also Cancel on the SignalBricks page and a connect that fails, so a dispatcher still configured with the old token in hubitat.json needs the new one after any of them. A registration that fails for a reason that may pass (not verified yet, SignalBricks or Hubitat cloud unavailable, timeout) is retried automatically after about 30 s, 2 min and 5 min, and the page shows the retry state. Debug > Refresh Access Token registers the new token. If SignalBricks can't be reached on Disconnect, the app disconnects itself and asks you to also disconnect the hub on its SignalBricks hub page. Once connected the page shows the organization and hub, Reconnect (replaces the token again and registers it) and Disconnect (SignalBricks deletes its copy, then the app replaces the token). The access token is no longer shown once the hub is connected. The app re-registers when you click Done and once after an update. The token, the PKCE verifier and the connect link are never logged. The existing endpoints (/sync, /info, /devices, /register) are unchanged. Requires OAuth enabled for the app code (HPM does this).
1.3.7 - New Bookings page, linked from the app page under Diagnostics (#29). It lists every booking the app knows (booking id, guest, check-in and checkout in hub time, and whether it is current, upcoming or past) and, for each of its locks, the slot that holds its code or "not on lock", matched the same way reconcile matches (prefix + ORB<booking id>, or a slot the app assigned earlier). It also lists orphans: codes with this app's prefix and an ORB booking id (or in a slot it assigned) that match no known booking for that lock, which the next reconcile removes. Codes still on a lock for an upcoming or past booking are flagged (reconcile removes them), and a lock that has never reported its codes shows "no codes reported". A summary line counts bookings known, codes on locks, current bookings not on a lock, and orphans, with the time and call (PUT /sync, PATCH /sync, or one booking's sync or delete) of the last booking sync, recorded from this version on and cleared by Reset State. Codes show only their last 2 digits; full codes are never shown or logged, and opening the page writes no log lines. The page reads only the hub's own state and the locks' last reported codes; it sends nothing and reads nothing from the locks. Door code writing, reconcile, code naming and the refresh are unchanged.
1.3.6 - Fixes "Failed to upgrade app" when updating to 1.3.5 on a hub that already has the app installed: the hub runs the app page while saving the code, and the new door code refresh section read app state that does not exist at that point. No other changes; everything in 1.3.5 below applies.
1.3.5 - Door code refresh no longer floods Z-Wave (#24). Up to 1.3.4 the app re-read every slot of every lock each night at midnight, starting a lock every 90 seconds, so on hubs with large locks the reads overlapped and Z-Wave timed out for hours. The refresh is now Off by default, also on hubs that update, and reads one lock at a time: the next lock starts when the current one reports its codes (not before 2.6 s per slot, at least 60 s, then 30 s to settle) or after its time budget (3 s per slot, 2 to 20 minutes). The app page has a new Door code refresh section: a Scheduled refresh setting (Off, Weekly on Tuesday or Daily, at a random time between 01:00 and 03:59 hub time, picked once per hub), a Refresh door codes now button for all locks or one chosen lock, and the progress of a running refresh. Clicking Done no longer starts a refresh. The old midnight schedule is removed when you click Done after updating, or the next time it fires (it then reads no lock). Door code writing, reconcile, code naming, the prefix and the minimum code position are unchanged.
1.3.4 - First release through Hubitat Package Manager. Hubs that installed the app by hand: use HPM Match Up (see the README), don't Install it again. The app page and log lines now show the app name with the version ("SignalBricks Integration 1.3.4"), the app has a description of what it does, the page warns when the code name prefix is empty, and explains that "Status: Not registered" is expected (the dispatcher drives the app through its endpoints; lock events reach SignalBricks through SignalBricks Telemetry). The "webhook: No SignalBricks ID" log line is now at trace level instead of debug. Door code writing, reconcile and code naming are unchanged; API responses still carry the bare version.
